top_story.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement sole-sources a three-year Hootsuite social media monitoring platform, value redacted
top_story.dek: The agency's justification says only Hootsuite can supply the platform, including an artificial intelligence tool trained on twelve years of social media data.
paragraphs: The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Office of Acquisition Management, part of the Department of Homeland Security, plans to buy Hootsuite Inc. Enterprise licenses and the Talkwalker platform for its Office of Public Affairs. The order goes through Carahsoft Technology Corp., the reseller on a Department of Homeland Security-wide agreement. The justification (J&A-26-0292) is filed as "items peculiar to one manufacturer," and the dollar amount is redacted in the posted copy. The planned period of performance runs September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2029, so it begins before the notice was posted on October 12.

The document says Hootsuite is the only vendor able to provide "proprietary AI capability unavailable from other sources," naming a tool called Wisdom "which has been trained on twelve years of historical social media data." It describes the platform as covering publishing, monitoring, listening, alerting, archiving and workflow approval across multiple social media accounts. A separate prior justification for Hootsuite Enterprise and the Talkwalker visual recognition tool at the same agency is also on file in this pipeline's vendor history.

Hootsuite is a commercial software company with federal contracts on record since 2011. The unusual part is the scope: a multi-year, single-vendor monitoring platform for the agency's public affairs office, justified by the vendor's own proprietary AI.

sections.headline: The Marine Barracks Washington buys sound, lighting and stage work for its Birthday Ball from the Washington Hilton's exclusive in-house vendor
paragraphs: 8 new sole-source justifications today, 3 of them posted as Special Notices rather than in the Justification category (Katmai, Encore and BD Biosciences); 1 repeat from an earlier edition was left out. The Hootsuite justification for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is today's Top Story and is not repeated in a card below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Marine Barracks Washington sole-sources audio-visual production for the Marine Corps Birthday Ball at the Washington Hilton
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Navy (Marine Barracks Washington)
blocks.text: The service is audio-visual, lighting, sound, video projection and stage support for the Marine Corps Birthday Ball on November 21, 2026. The justification says the Hilton "maintains an exclusive contract with Encore Global as its sole authorized in-house audiovisual and production provider," and that outside vendors would have to subcontract through Encore. Market research consisted of correspondence with the hotel's events department and Encore's listing on the Hilton's event-services webpage. The document says the Marine Barracks will look for competitive providers at future events held at other venues. Posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Army surgical research institute gets a no-compete IT bridge contract for its incumbent contractor
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Defense Health Agency contracting activity, on behalf of the U.S. Army Institute of Surgical Research, plans a new bridge contract for IT support: tier II desktop, radiology and imaging system administration, virtual machine infrastructure and SharePoint. The notice says Katmai, as the incumbent, "is the only source that currently possesses the operational infrastructure, knowledge, and experience," and that any other contractor would cause "a lapse in service, and significant loss of data." A bridge to the incumbent means the replacement contract was not in place before the current one expires. Responses were due six days after publication. Posted as a Special Notice.

sections.headline: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration's commercial space station contract carries a $34 billion ceiling
paragraphs: 29 new solicitations, plus several documents read today on notices posted earlier; 6 were flagged and 23 are routine. It is a heavy day because attachments on notices posted in September and early October were read for the first time, and four of them clear the bar.

blocks.title: NASA opens the Commercial Low Earth Orbit Destination Contract with a $34.06 billion ceiling
meta: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Johnson Space Center)
blocks.text: From the request for proposals, read today on a notice posted earlier: "the contract guaranteed minimum amount to be ordered under this contract is $100,000,000 and the contract Not-to-Exceed (NTE) amount* which may be ordered under this contract shall not exceed $34,063,000,000." The contractor must be a "United States Commercial Provider." It must consent to the government collecting remotely-sensed data on the station and visiting vehicles. It must not contract with China or Chinese-owned companies except for commercial and non-developmental items. A deliverables attachment also requires disclosing any use of "Super Intelligence" across the station's lifecycle.

blocks.title: Coast Guard solicits a new Light Icebreaker (Homeland Security Cutter) in a two-phase competition
blocks.text: From the request for proposals, read today: the government "intends to utilize a two-phase advisory down-select process." Shipyards must describe "Capability for concurrent production of up to four vessels simultaneously" and the ability to launch a vessel with the characteristics of the substantially complete icebreaker.

blocks.title: Coast Guard seeks a production line for the third-generation Response Boat-Small, with a demonstration boat from each awardee
blocks.text: The request for proposals describes an indefinite-delivery contract for a complete Response Boat-Small III with trailer and equipment. After award, "an initial Delivery Order will be issued to each awardee for one (1) boat" for an in-water demonstration. Offerors must also show they can meet a production rate of "upwards of 60 boats per year." Read today on a notice posted earlier.

footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported, and the OMB section listed no known gaps. Of 492 attachments on 93 SAM.gov notices, 12 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, 1 has no extractable text (video/CAD), and 392 are queued and will be read in later editions, so findings from them may appear later as late document findings. The Microsoft justification for the Department of Homeland Security had only the notice text and no attached document. About 1,397 links to outside portals (1,364 to the Defense Logistics Agency's DIBBS) were not followed.
